hypothesis: If the claim holds, a public account of living elephants says the trunk is a nostril, that the trunk brings food and water to the mouth, and that the trunk coils around or pulls up trees or stems.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported). All three components are supported by at least one sentence in the combined text of the Animal Diversity Web accounts of Loxodonta africana and Elephas maximus and the ElephantVoices trunk-behavior pages linked from the ethogram index. Nostril: the sentence contains trunk or proboscis, and nostril, nose, or nasal. Food and drink: the sentence contains trunk or proboscis, mouth, and food, water, or drink. Trees: the sentence contains trunk or proboscis, and tree, stem, or branch, and coil, wrap, uproot, tear, or pull. A sentence split on period, exclamation mark or question mark is the unit.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. A component is refuted only by a sentence that contains the same content words and also says does not, cannot, or never. The claim is refuted if every component is refuted. It is mixed if at least one component is supported and at least one is refuted. A component with neither a support sentence nor a denial is untested. If any component is untested, the verdict is inconclusive with reason underpowered. If none of the three pages can be downloaded, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. A checksum mismatch on a re-download of a page, after the HTML processing-time or session token is left as-is only when the normalized text hash matches, is not by itself a failure; the normalized visible text is what is hashed.

test_contract.expected_observation: At least one sentence identifies the trunk as a nostril or nose, at least one says the trunk brings food or water to the mouth, and at least one says the trunk coils around, wraps, pulls, tears or uproots a tree, stem or branch.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A sentence that denies one of those three acts or denies that the trunk is a nostril. Silence is not a denial.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Public natural-history accounts of living elephants (Elephantidae) that describe the trunk in prose. The accounts must not be Aristotle's text. Video that cannot be transcribed in this run does not count. Both living genera are in scope; one genus is enough to support an existence claim about elephants, and an explicit denial for both genera would be required to refute.
test_contract.inference_method: Split the visible text into sentences. Score each sentence with the keyword rules above. A component is supported by one matching sentence and refuted only by a denial. All three supported and none refuted yields supports. Any untested component yields inconclusive underpowered.

interpretation: The sentence says three things: the proboscis is a nostril, it is used as a hand to bring food and fluid to the mouth, and it tears up trees by coiling around their stems. 'As a hand' is read through those acts, not through a count of manipulative neurons. The test looks for the three acts in modern natural-history prose. It does not measure how often they occur.
confidence_rule_preregistered: All three components supported and none denied: 0.6. Mixed: 0.45. Inconclusive: 0.35. The ceiling is 0.6 because the data are prose accounts, not a counted sample of behavior.
caveats: Criteria were written before the account pages were downloaded. Only the HTTP status of the three landing URLs was checked.
Keyword sentences can match a negation that does not use the words does not, cannot or never. Any such sentence is quoted in the output so the match can be checked.

The ethogram index links to the library at /ethogram, and the trunk-behavior pages are the library cards that contain the word trunk or proboscis. Site navigation, the footer and the cookie dialog were not scored. Keyword matches include sentences that mention the words without describing the act; each matched sentence is in derived/matched-sentences.csv. The SHA-256 on each file is the hash of the normalized visible main text. raw_sha256 is the HTML bytes, which can change when the page template changes.

The nostril denial is one sentence on the Silly-Trunk page. It calls the trunk a long nose and says the infant does not know what to make of it. The pre-registered rule counts every sentence that has the content words and also says does not, cannot, or never as a denial, so the nostril component is not a clean support.

measured.uncertainty: nostril=both (3 support, 1 denial); food=supported (9 support, 0 denial); trees=supported (4 support, 0 denial)

supports: Using their trunks as a temporary container or holding, African elephants use their trunks to gather water and shoot it into their mouths.
An elephant submerging its trunk or mouth under water and purposefully and/or repeatedly blowing bubbles.
An individual sucking water into its trunk and pouring it into its mouth.
In some cases, with unskilled calves, or individuals with injured trunks, kneeling down to suck water directly into the mouth.
In addition to such sampling, infants and young calves may also sample what adults are eating by placing their trunk in the mouths the mouths of older elephants and pulling out food items.
Picking up a potential food item with the trunk, and placing it in the mouth and possibly chewing it begins around the age or one to two months.
Grasping a branch with the trunk and pulling it downward over a tusk and, simultaneously lifting the head and tusk upward to break the branch.
Grasping a branch or branchlet with the trunk, pulling and breaking it.
Using the trunk to feel about under water for a suitable plant, grasping its stems with the trunk and pulling to uproot it.
Grasping a seedling with the trunk and, using the strength of the trunk alone, breaking the stem, or uprooting the seedling, and placing the partial or entire plant into the mouth.

method: Downloaded the Animal Diversity Web accounts of Loxodonta africana and Elephas maximus and the ElephantVoices ethogram index. The index links to the ethogram library. Every library card whose title or preview contains trunk or proboscis was downloaded and its main-text sentences were scored. A listed word matches itself and the regular inflections -s, -es, -ed and -ing, and does not match a longer stem such as branchlet, vomeronasal or seedling. A sentence with the content words supports that component unless it also says does not, cannot, or never, in which case it denies the component. Scored 161 pages (159 trunk-behavior pages). Failed fetches: 0.
results_summary: Nostril: both. Support: "An audible exhalation of air through the trunk that appears to be made for the purpose of clearing the nasal passages." Denial: "It does seem as if the infant does not know what to make of its long nose and Silly-Trunk is part of the infants learning how to use and control it."
Food and drink: supported. Support: "Using their trunks as a temporary container or holding, African elephants use their trunks to gather water and shoot it into their mouths."
Trees: supported. Support: "Grasping a branch with the trunk and pulling it downward over a tusk and, simultaneously lifting the head and tusk upward to break the branch."
Verdict mixed. 2 of 3 components supported without a denial. 161 pages scored.
